package_info.why_malicious: The entire repository can be made to appear trustworthy by forging commit metadata (timestamps and contributor identities), misleading developers into trusting and using code that may be malicious. This undermines the integrity of the software supply chain and can be used to distribute malicious code under the guise of reputable contributors and long-standing activity.

execution_context.file_location: N/A (executed in terminal before committing code)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
set git GIT_AUTHOR_DATE=2010-04-19 17:18:43
set git GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2010-04-19 17:18:43
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Before committing, the code sets environment variables to falsify the commit timestamp, making the commit appear as if it was made in the past, thus fabricating a false history of activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Manipulating commit timestamps is not a normal part of development and is used to create a deceptive history.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal commits should reflect the actual time of code changes; this behavior forges historical activity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, developers may backdate commits for migration or archival purposes, but this is not standard practice.
key_indicators: Unusual or impossible commit dates (e.g., before repo/user creation)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
git config user.name <spoofed_username>
git config user.email <spoofed_email>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Before committing, the code sets the git username and email to those of a reputable third party, causing the commit to be falsely attributed to that person.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Attributing commits to someone else without their knowledge is a clear sign of deception and potential social engineering.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal commits should be attributed to the actual author; this behavior forges contributor identity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, a team may use a shared account for automation, but impersonating real users is not legitimate.
key_indicators: Commits from a user/email not associated with the actual committer's account
Contributor list includes well-known users who have no public association with the project

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After setting forged metadata, the code commits changes, creating a commit with falsified author and timestamp information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Committing with forged metadata is the final step in creating a deceptive project history.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal commits should reflect true authorship and timing; this is used to mislead users.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Standard commit command, but contextually suspicious when preceded by metadata forgery.
key_indicators: Commits with mismatched or implausible metadata
Commit history inconsistent with actual project activity

attack_chain.action: Attacker collects email addresses of reputable GitHub users by scraping public commit patches.
Attacker sets local git config to spoof username and email of reputable users.
Attacker sets environment variables to falsify commit timestamps, creating a fake history of activity.
Attacker commits code with forged metadata, populating the repository with fake contributors and activity.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository appears highly active and reputable, increasing likelihood of trust and adoption

attack_chain.action: Developers and users are deceived by the falsified metadata, potentially using or installing malicious code from the repository.

behavioral_signatures: Commits with author dates predating repository or user creation
Bulk commits with identical or sequentially backdated timestamps
Commits attributed to well-known users who have no public association with the project
Contributor lists with suspiciously high-profile or unrelated users
file_indicators: No direct file indicators; detection relies on metadata analysis
network_indicators: No direct network indicators; attack is local and metadata-based
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor commit metadata for anomalies such as author dates before repository/user creation, bulk backdated commits, and contributors with no public association to the project. Flag repositories with a high number of unsigned commits or with contributors who are well-known but have no public record of involvement. Encourage and enforce commit signature verification and vigilant mode to help identify and prevent metadata forgery.
